title: Code walkthrough (cw/1)
description: One pull request or one subsystem, split into parts, sections and steps. This file is the whole content of a walkthrough: a reader holds no topic of its own. The format is meant to outlive any one reader, so a consumer renders the blocks it understands and skips the rest without complaining.

$schema.description: Path or URL to this schema, so an editor validates the file while it is being written.

version.description: The format this file is written in. A consumer that does not know the version refuses the file rather than guessing at it.

title.description: The heading in the page header. For a pull request, its title.

summary.description: The paragraph on the overview, above the cards. What the change does and why, in a few sentences.

root.description: The checkout every file path is relative to. The command line --root wins over this, and without either a local reader uses the repository the walkthrough file sits in. Only used for opening files and for checking that the pasted code still matches the tree.

language.description: Fallback language for code blocks that do not name one.

parts.description: The chapters of the walkthrough. Three to six is the working range: the overview is a set of cards, not a list to scroll.

source.description: Where the walkthrough comes from, in a form a machine can act on. It is what turns a file path plus a line number into a link, so a consumer that wants to point at the original needs nothing else.

kind.description: What is being explained. pull-request is the common case and the only one that carries a diff.

provider.description: Who hosts it. A consumer that does not know the provider falls back to url and stops there.

repo.description: Owner and name, the way the provider writes it.

number.description: The pull request or ticket, written the way it should read in the header. The machine-readable form lives in url.

url.description: The pull request, commit or page this walkthrough is about.

state.description: Small chip next to the number.

commit.description: The commit every snippet was taken from. This is what makes a permalink permanent, so leaving it out costs the reader the ability to see the code in context.

base.description: The branch the change merges into.

head.description: The branch the change is on.

changedFiles.description: The paths this change touches. A consumer uses it to tell a snippet of changed code from a snippet of untouched context, and to link the first into the diff.

title.description: The card heading. A claim, not a category.

desc.description: One line on the card, under the title.

long.description: The paragraph on the part page itself, where there is room for the why.

files.description: File name chips on the card. Basenames read better here than full paths.

sections.description: The rows on the part page. Each one is a run of steps about a single idea.

desc.description: One line on the row, under the title.

steps.description: Two to five steps. A section with one step is a step; a section with nine is two sections.

step.description: One screen, written for a technical reader. Prose always, and then whichever of diagram, code, diff and anim earn their place. A step with prose alone is allowed and should be rare.

body.description: The explanation, for someone who reads code. Two or three sentences on what happens and why it is done this way.

speech.description: The same step said out loud, for a consumer that reads the walkthrough rather than showing it. Only worth writing when body leans on what is on screen: 'the highlighted line' means nothing in an ear. Left out, a reader falls back to body.

callout.description: The warn block under the step. For the thing that will bite the next person, not for emphasis.

diagram.description: A mermaid diagram. Blocks named in refs become clickable and show the code behind them.

def.description: Mermaid source. Newlines as \n, the way mermaid would read it from a file.

caption.description: The line under the diagram. One sentence saying what to take away from it.

refs.description: Keyed by the node id or the exact node label in the mermaid source. Clicking that block opens the code below the diagram.

label.description: What the panel calls this block. Defaults to the key.

note.description: Why this block is worth opening, in one sentence.

code.description: The lines to show. Short: this is a peek from a diagram, not the snippet panel.
A snippet, shown with its own gutter. Line numbers in hi, add and notes are the numbers the gutter shows: 1 upwards, or from upwards when from is set.

to.description: The last line of the snippet in the file. Redundant with from plus the line count, and worth stating anyway: it is what a link to a line range needs, and a consumer resolving the code live can check it before it reads.

lang.description: Overrides the walkthrough-level language for this snippet.

note.description: The chip next to the file name.

text.description: The code itself. A copy, kept so the walkthrough reads without a checkout; sha and to are what let a consumer with a checkout prefer the real thing.

hi.description: Lines to light up. The ones the step is actually about.

add.description: Lines this change adds, marked with a + and a green wash.

notes.description: A marker on a line that opens a sentence. For what the code does not say on its own.

diff.description: A before and after. Not verifiable against a tree: half of it is by definition no longer there.

kind.description: ctx keeps the line on both sides, add is only on the right, del only on the left.

t.description: The line, without the leading + or -.

anim.description: A handful of states played in a loop. For something that happens over time and has no code to point at: a rollout, a retry ladder, a migration window. A consumer that cannot animate shows the frames in order, or skips the block.

label.description: Where on the clock this frame is.

note.description: What changed since the frame before.

nodes.description: The same nodes in the same order in every frame. Only their state changes.

sub.description: The second line, for a time or a status.

state.description: idle is waiting, active is happening now, done has happened, gone has been removed, alert is the failure this frame is about. Defaults to idle.

check.description: What the publisher's working tree said about this snippet when the walkthrough was published. It is provenance, not content: a consumer with the repository in front of it works the same thing out for itself from sha, and one without it can at least say whether the paste was already out of date when it was written down.

state.description: ok means the lines were where the snippet says they are. moved means they were found elsewhere in the file, which is not the same as changed. gone means they were not in the file at all. unchecked means there was no working tree to compare against.

line.description: Where the lines actually started, when that is not where from says.

ext.description: The one open place in an otherwise closed schema. For data a particular consumer needs and the format has no opinion about. Anything here is ignored by every consumer that did not put it there, so nothing a reader needs to work belongs in it.

id.description: A name for this part, section or step that survives editing. Progress, bookmarks and deep links hang off it, so inserting a step must not renumber the ones around it. Left out, a publisher derives one from the title and writes it back.

path.description: Repository-relative path with forward slashes. It is what a link or an open button hands on, so it has to be real.

sha1.description: A git object name, full or abbreviated to at least seven characters.

sha256.description: sha256 over the snippet text with CRLF folded to LF and trailing newlines removed. A consumer with a checkout compares it against the file to see whether the paste is still the truth, without having to diff the text.
